options.text: Each term is $7$ more than the one before, because we keep adding $7$.
The list looks neat, so it is a pattern even with no rule stated.
The same add-$7$ rule explains why $35$ comes next after $28$.
The same list also proves a new theorem about every infinite sequence.

stem:
Esha counts floor tiles laid in a strip: $7$, $14$, $21$, $28$, $\ldots$

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims treat the list as a mathematical pattern?

teacher.key_rationale: A mathematical pattern needs a clear regularity and a reason it continues; here each term grows by adding 7, which also yields 35 next. Neat looks alone omit the rule. Stretching the strip into a theorem about every sequence overreaches the chapter.
